_comment: W1331 ratchet baseline -- see tests/test_w1331_disclosure_branch_symmetry.py. Every entry is a command that routes a disclosure signal to one output branch and not another, so a consumer of the other branch reads a degraded run as a clean one. This list may only SHRINK: the test fails both on a new violation and on a stale entry. Every entry names a reason code from _reason_codes; adding a code, or an entry, is a reviewable diff by construction.
_high_water_mark_note: Raised 52 -> 68 when the W1455 scanner rebuild added the SARIF-artifact rule: a disclosure printed as text BESIDE a SARIF document is not disclosure IN the document, so 16 commands that json and text both disclose are blind in the artifact a CI system actually ingests. The 16 are real findings the previous scanner could not see, not a relaxation -- every pre-existing entry still reproduces and none were dropped. The mark may only fall from here.

_reason_codes.structured-envelope-instead-of-exit: DELIBERATE and pinned by a test: the JSON branch answers a resolution failure with a structured envelope (partial_success, state, error) and exit 0, because a non-zero exit strips the structured signal at the MCP wrapper -- see the Pattern-1B/1C note in cmd_diagnose.py and test_cmd_why_resolution.py's explicit assert exit_code == 0. The text branch has no envelope to carry the signal, so it uses the exit code instead. Not a defect; do not 'fix' by making --json exit non-zero without changing those tests.
